data.title: Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly with Subsequent Account Changes
data.description: Detects financial institution employees accessing customer accounts outside their normal behavioral pattern, combined with subsequent account modifications — a hallmark of insider- enabled fraud. The rule identifies four converging anomaly signals: (1) account access occurring outside normal business hours for the employee's role, (2) access volume significantly exceeding the employee's baseline, (3) access to accounts not assigned to the employee's portfolio or branch, and (4) account changes (address, beneficiary, contact info, transaction limits) following the anomalous access. The ACFE estimates insider fraud accounts for 5% of organizational revenue globally, with an average detection time of 18 months. Financial institution insiders are particularly dangerous because they understand internal controls and operate below detection thresholds. This rule correlates UEBA access data with account modification logs to surface the positioning phase (CFPF P3) before funds are extracted.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_portfolio_mismatch AND (filter_after_hours OR filter_volume_anomaly) AND filter_subsequent_modification

enrichment_required.source: UEBA baseline — rolling 30-day average daily account access count per employee
CRM/core banking assignment — whether account is assigned to the accessing employee
Account modification audit log correlated within 24 hours of anomalous access

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly
// Detects out-of-portfolio access with after-hours or volume anomaly followed by account changes
(event_type="account_view" OR event_type="account_detail_access" OR event_type="account_modification")
account_in_employee_portfolio="false"
(access_time_local<"08:00" OR access_time_local>"18:00" OR daily_account_access_count>=baseline*3)
account_modification_within_24h="true"
| access_to_modification_minutes := dateDiff(modification_timestamp, access_timestamp, unit=minutes)
| baseline_deviation := daily_account_access_count / baseline_daily_access
| groupBy(employee_id, function=[
    collect([account_id, event_type, access_timestamp, modification_type,
             modification_timestamp, access_to_modification_minutes,
             employee_branch, source_ip, workstation_id]),
    count(account_id, distinct=true, as=unique_accounts_accessed)
  ])
| sort(unique_accounts_accessed, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly")`
`comment("Detects out-of-portfolio account access with anomalous timing/volume followed by modifications")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:employee_audit
  (event_type="account_view" OR event_type="account_detail_access" OR event_type="account_modification")
  account_in_employee_portfolio="false"
| eval hour = strftime(_time, "%H")
| eval after_hours = if(hour < 8 OR hour > 18, 1, 0)
| stats dc(account_id) AS unique_accounts count AS total_events
    sum(after_hours) AS after_hours_events
    values(modification_type) AS modifications
    values(account_id) AS accounts_accessed
    BY employee_id, employee_role, employee_branch
| where unique_accounts > 10 OR after_hours_events > 0
| lookup employee_baseline employee_id OUTPUT baseline_daily_access
| eval deviation_multiple = unique_accounts / baseline_daily_access
| where deviation_multiple >= 3 OR after_hours_events > 0
| eval risk_score = case(
    deviation_multiple >= 5 AND after_hours_events > 3 AND isnotnull(modifications), "critical",
    deviation_multiple >= 3 AND isnotnull(modifications), "high",
    after_hours_events > 0 AND isnotnull(modifications), "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table employee_id, employee_role, employee_branch, unique_accounts,
        deviation_multiple, after_hours_events, modifications,
        accounts_accessed, risk_score
| sort - risk_score
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly
-- Detects out-of-portfolio access + anomalous patterns + subsequent account changes
WITH access_events AS (
  SELECT
    ea.employee_id,
    ea.employee_role,
    ea.employee_branch,
    ea.account_id,
    ea.event_type,
    ea.access_timestamp,
    CASE WHEN DATEPART(HOUR, ea.access_timestamp) < 8
          OR DATEPART(HOUR, ea.access_timestamp) > 18
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS after_hours_flag,
    eb.baseline_daily_access
  FROM employee_audit_log ea
  JOIN employee_baselines eb ON ea.employee_id = eb.employee_id
  LEFT JOIN employee_portfolio ep ON ea.employee_id = ep.employee_id
    AND ea.account_id = ep.account_id
  WHERE ea.access_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
    AND ep.account_id IS NULL  -- not in employee portfolio
),
employee_summary AS (
  SELECT
    employee_id,
    employee_role,
    employee_branch,
    COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS unique_accounts_accessed,
    SUM(after_hours_flag) AS after_hours_events,
    MAX(baseline_daily_access) AS baseline_daily_access,
    CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(MAX(baseline_daily_access), 0) AS deviation_multiple
  FROM access_events
  GROUP BY employee_id, employee_role, employee_branch
),
modifications AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    am.employee_id,
    am.account_id,
    am.modification_type,
    am.modification_timestamp
  FROM account_modifications am
  WHERE am.modification_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT
  es.*,
  m.modification_type,
  m.account_id AS modified_account
FROM employee_summary es
JOIN modifications m ON es.employee_id = m.employee_id
WHERE es.deviation_multiple >= 3 OR es.after_hours_events > 0
ORDER BY es.deviation_multiple DESC

references: ACFE, Report to the Nations (2024) — occupational fraud statistics, 18-month median detection time
CERT National Insider Threat Center, Common Sense Guide to Mitigating Insider Threats
FDIC, Enforcement Decisions — insider fraud cases
DOJ, Bank fraud prosecution records — insider collusion patterns
falsepositives: Managers or team leads covering for absent employees and accessing their portfolio accounts
System administrators performing authorized bulk account maintenance or data migration
Employees recently transferred to a new branch accessing accounts from their previous portfolio
Authorized after-hours processing during month-end, quarter-end, or regulatory reporting cycles
